design: Shock-Cohort Residual Reversal (SCRR): on the PIT 273-asset true-daily OHLCV panel, flag asset-days where the beta-shrunk market-residual return is |z_e| >= 2.5 (range-vol standardised) AND the day's range or volume is extreme; fit a hierarchical/monotone-GBM slope kappa_h for the fraction of the shock-day residual that reverses over h in {1,3,5} days; at the shock-day close go LONG the loser cohort (Arm A, BTC-short beta hedge; Arm B long-losers/short-winners), size by (m_i - cost)/(lambda h sigma^2) under caps, hold to t+h with no re-trim; score with unmodified trader.backtest.cell_metrics at 21/30 bp plus a declared borrow term. Profit claimed as a first-moment forecast of the post-shock residual (liquidity-provision premium, Nagel 2012); learning justified by partial pooling across assets, sign-flipping range x volume x dispersion interactions, and multi-horizon sharing. Kill: Stage 0 slope table (kappa_3(event) >= 0.08, date-clustered t >= 3, above non-event slope and a circular-shift placebo), then a frozen book on the 2024-01 -> 2026-06 hold-out and the full 2019-2026 span.
lens: NO-FREE-LUNCH / ARITHMETIC (cost identity, breadth, per-event edge vs 21 bp at the mechanism's real turnover, SR0(N), power on unseen years, whether the 'learning' beats a closed-form slope)
strongest_objection: The mechanism's profit source and its cost are the same quantity, and the experiment as designed cannot tell them apart. It invokes the liquidity-provision premium (Nagel 2012) but EXECUTES as a liquidity TAKER at the shock-day close: the premium — the widened spread and the intraday bounce after forced flow — has by then been paid to whoever posted bids during the cascade. What the daily close-to-close residual still shows as 'reversal' on illiquid alts is bounded by the spread the taker must pay to enter, and the equity anchor's own rebuttals say exactly this: Atkins-Dyl 1990 ('the magnitude of the overreaction is small compared to the bid-ask spreads', abstract fetched), Cox-Peterson 1994 ('the bid-ask bounce and the degree of market liquidity explain short-term price reversals'; large one-day losers 'perform poorly over an extended time horizon', abstract fetched), and Bremer-Sweeney 1991's own abstract ('while perhaps not representing abnormal profit opportunities', fetched). The design's Stage-0 PASS threshold kappa_3 >= 0.08 lies inside the bid-ask-bounce band for Kraken alts (a 25-100 bp sell-driven close on a 12.5% shock is kappa 0.02-0.08 of pure bounce, unharvestable by a taker). In this repo the reversal premium's measured home is already known: 806 `persistence` IC -0.052 / `linear_uni` +0.057 at H=1 min (real reversal), 897 0/864 at any nonzero fee (cost-bound) — the daily residual is what is left after makers harvested it. The only crypto daily-overreaction evidence I could fetch (Caporale-Plastun 2019, BTC/LTC/XRP/DASH, abstract-level) reads the opposite sign: next-day moves after overreaction days are LARGER in both directions, the contrarian strategy is 'not profitable', and 'the overreactions ... do not give rise to exploitable profit opportunities (possibly because of transaction costs)'. To clear +0.97 net the design's own arithmetic needs kappa >= 0.10 on essentially EVERY event cohort (K ~ 94/yr, turnover 0.10/day — only 1.5x below the trend book, not the advertised 3.5x) or kappa >= 0.18-0.20 on 10-15 cascade cohorts/yr whose 2024-26 supply is ~5-10 and which the 2.5-yr hold-out cannot certify (t ~ 1.4). Under the goalposts' 'unseen years, CI lo > 0' the mechanism is structurally unverifiable: the hold-out CI half-width at the bar is +-1.5 or worse, and the full-span CI the design falls back on includes the fitted years.
arithmetic_check: (1) EVENT SUPPLY. |z_e| >= 2.5 on fat-tailed residuals standardised by a 30-d range vol: unit-variance t(3) gives P(|z|>2.5) = P(|T3| > 4.33) ~ 2.2%, t(4) ~ 2.5%, normal 1.24%. RZ >= 2 (range twice the 30-d median) is almost implied by a 12.5% close-to-close move on an asset whose median range is 6-8%, while VZ >= 2 means volume >= e^2 = 7.4x median (the two thresholds are on different scales, ratio vs log). So 'either' ~ range-only ~ the bare |z_e| >= 2.5 set: the 'event' IS the tail of the lag-1 residual return, an F1 feature with a threshold. Supply ~ 250 x 365 x 2% ~ 1800 asset-events/yr on 2024-26 (design assumed 900-1400); more events, but no new information source. (2) PER-EVENT ECONOMICS reproduced: |e| = 12.5% (2.5 sigma at sigma = 5%); kappa 0.10 -> gross 1.25%, net@21 0.83% (42 bp RT = 34% of gross), net@30 0.65% (48%), net@40 0.45% (64%). 3-d position sd ~10% (GARCH-elevated ~6%/d x sqrt3): SR_pos 0.083 / 0.065 / 0.045; cohort n=12, rho=0.25 -> x1.79 -> SR_e 0.15 / 0.12 / 0.08 before hedge carry (18-36 bp on beta-notional, ~-0.02): the design's SR_e ~0.10 at kappa 0.10 is consistent. SR_yr = SR_e sqrt(K) is correct for a book flat outside cohorts (flat days add zero mean and ~zero variance under cell_metrics' mean/std x sqrt(365) at H=1, trader/backtest.py). Bar +0.97: K = 94 (SR_e 0.10), 42 (0.15), 9.2 (0.32). On cascade days rho ~0.5 is more plausible for a cohort selected on 'fell most on the same day' (shared exposure to the failed entity): sqrt(12/6.5) = 1.36 instead of 1.79 -> SR_e down 24%, K up 1.7x. (3) TURNOVER CLAIM IS INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT: '0.044/day, 3.5x fewer cost events' uses K=40 x 0.2 gross x 2 = 16 units/yr, but K=40 at SR_e 0.10 gives SR_yr 0.63 < bar. At the bar-clearing K=94: 37.6 units/yr = 0.103/day, 1.5x below the trend book's 0.152 (POWERED_RESULT FULL turn), fee bill 7.9%/yr vs 11.9%. Sparsity buys ~4%/yr, not an order of magnitude. (4) BOUNCE VS PREMIUM: a sell-driven last trade at the bid, exit near mid/ask, contributes ~one spread to the measured close-to-close reversal. Kraken alt spreads (order of magnitude, unverified — 907 measured BTC/USD only): 20-100 bp calm, wider on cascade days. On a 12.5% shock that is kappa_bounce 0.02-0.08 — the S0 PASS band (0.08). Harvestable kappa = kappa_measured - kappa_bounce, and the taker pays the same spread on entry: with shock-day half-spread 25-75 bp/side the honest RT cost is 2 x (16 + 25..75) = 82-182 bp, so kappa 0.10 nets +0.43..-0.57% and kappa 0.20 nets +0.7..+1.7% per position. Positivity alone needs kappa_harvestable >= 0.15-0.20; the bar then needs K >= 40-90 cohorts/yr at that kappa — every event, not the cascade dozen. (5) CASCADE SUPPLY: market-wide crash days I can name on 2024-26 (2024-03-05, 04-13, 08-05, 12-19; 2025-02-03, 02-25/28, 04-07, 10-10; 2026 unknown to me) ~5-10/yr. At SR_e 0.32 (kappa 0.20): 7/yr -> SR_yr 0.85 < bar; ~20 cohorts on the hold-out -> t = 0.32 sqrt(20) = 1.4, undetectable. The cascade arm cannot be certified on unseen data at any kappa the literature supports. (6) POWER: SE(SR_hat) over T yrs is sqrt((1 + SR^2/2)/T) (Lo 2002) = 0.77 at SR ~1, T = 2.5 — the design used the SR = 0 value 0.63; half-width +-1.52, and the excess-kurtosis term of an event-lumpy book (say kurt_ex ~6: + (kurt_ex/4) SR^2 in the numerator) pushes SE to ~1.0, half-width ~+-2. Placebo Sharpes carry the same SE, so criterion (b) 'hold-out >= +0.56 AND placebo pct >= 95' binds at a realised SR >= ~1.3-1.6: power ~35-40% when the truth equals the bar. Criterion (c) full-span CI lo > 0 (needs SR > 0.72) includes 2019-23 where kappa was fitted — contaminated. No combination of the pass criteria gives a clean unseen-years verdict at the bar. (7) LEARNING: asset random effect a_i with <= 20 events and per-event y sd ~2 sigma-units has SE 2/sqrt(20) = 0.45 against an effect of 0.3 (kappa 0.10 x |z| 3): REML drives tau^2 to ~0 and everything shrinks to the pooled slope; four interaction slopes on ~150-300 clustered dates carry t ~1-2 each at plausible sizes. The learned object is a 1-5 parameter WLS; the GBM arm and hierarchical layer add reads (2 classes x 36 cells x 2 arms x hedged/unhedged x 2 accountings ~ 576) without information. (8) CONSISTENCY WITH E-2: kappa 0.10 on 2% of rows at |z| ~3 contributes pooled Pearson IC ~ 0.02 x 3 x 0.3/(1 x 2) ~ 0.009 — under E-2's floor, so E-2 cannot exclude it (the design is right), but TASK_915's threshold-capable GBM on F1 will see it if it exists: the event-conditional estimator adds POWER, not information — an appendix statistic, not a mechanism. (9) SR0(36) reproduced: Phi^-1(1-1/36) = 1.915, Phi^-1(1-1/(36e)) = 2.319, (0.4228)(1.915) + (0.5772)(2.319) = 2.148; x0.63 = 1.35, x0.37 = 0.79 — arithmetic correct, SD understated per (6).
profit_source_check: Labelled honestly as ONE source — a forecast of the conditional first moment of the h-day market-residual return given an extreme lag-1 residual — and correctly NOT counted as a rebalancing or market premium (hold-to-horizon, beta-hedged). Two dishonesties remain. (a) The economics invoked (liquidity provision) is a premium paid to those who SUPPLY liquidity at the bid during the cascade; the control law CONSUMES liquidity at the shock-day close, so the premium is the spread it pays, not the return it earns. The design's own citations locate the premium where it cannot be taken: Kitron 2026 (design's citation, abstract-level) — reversal 'emerges after aggressive taker flow' at 15 min, 1.3 bp gross vs 5 bp cost; the repo's 806 result (`persistence` IC -0.052, `linear_uni` +0.057 at H=1 min, runs/806_predictability_probe/result.md:29-35) and 897 (0/864 at any nonzero fee): a real minute-scale reversal that is cost-bound. The daily close-to-close residual is what remains after makers harvested it, and the equity anchor's rebuttals (Atkins-Dyl 1990, Cox-Peterson 1994, abstracts fetched) attribute that remainder to bid-ask bounce and liquidity. (b) 'Sparse turnover = cost avoidance that makes the forecast harvestable' is true only at K = 40, where the design's own arithmetic does not reach the bar; at the bar the turnover is 0.10/day, 1.5x below the trend book. Is it a forecast of something already measured dead? Not cleanly: the lag-1 return (lag1, lag1 x vol10, threshold-capable GBM/MLP) was in 819 CAPACITY's feature set on 20 majors 2024-07 -> 2025-08 and read IC ~0, but that pooled Pearson instrument cannot exclude a 2%-of-rows conditional kappa of 0.1 (arithmetic item 8) — so 'unmeasured on the PIT daily panel' is fair. What IS measured and points against it: Caporale-Plastun 2019 (crypto, 4 majors, abstract fetched) — next-day moves after overreaction days are larger in both directions, contrarian 'not profitable', no exploitable opportunity 'possibly because of transaction costs'; Liu-Tsyvinski 2018/2021 (NBER w24877, abstract fetched) — 'a strong time-series momentum effect' in crypto (horizon not in abstract; weekly per recollection, unverified). Literature the design leans on and I could not verify this session: Bianchi-Babiak-Dickerson 2022 (403; abstract-level via the design's own fetch — premium 'concentrated in pairs with lower market activity', i.e., where the spread is widest: the premium and the cost co-locate), Nagel 2012 (NBER w17653 abstract fetched: qualitative claims confirmed, no magnitudes; his reversal strategies are gross-of-cost equity portfolios, recollection), Bremer-Sweeney magnitude (RePEc abstract fetched: adjustment 'lasts approximately two days', 'perhaps not representing abnormal profit opportunities', no percentage — the kappa ~0.18 anchor stays unverified and the paper's own authors disclaim exploitability).

surviving_mechanism: None as a mechanism or a queue row. The narrowest surviving object is a MEASUREMENT, not a trader: a Stage-0 conditional-slope table run as an appendix statistic inside TASK_915's data build (same panel, same residual/vol-standardised target, ~2 CPU-hours, no GPU, no book) — kappa_h(event) vs kappa_h(non-event) for h in {1,3,5}, date-clustered, circular-shift placebo — WITH the four controls the design lacks: (i) a skip-day variant (enter at close t+1) as the bid-ask-bounce control; (ii) a liquidity-tercile split with BTC/ETH/top-tercile read separately (bounce ~0 there; note bounce and the Bianchi premium both scale with illiquidity, so the bottom tercile cannot separate them); (iii) a shock-day execution-cost proxy from the 1-minute table already in the DB (|close - last-15-min VWAP|, last-minute range on event days) reported in place of slip5; (iv) a BTC-only post-cascade series as the market-timing control for the beta-hedged cohort. PASS (kappa_3,skip >= 0.10 on the top-liquidity tercile, t >= 3, above placebo p95) licenses at most an event indicator as an F3 interaction inside TASK_915's GBM cell — not a separate book, not a learned policy. FAIL closes the 'IC concentrated on regime days' escape hatch for TASK_915's G-A. This is a slope with two controls, i.e. a closed-form estimator; it is not the learning mechanism the operator asked for, and saying so is part of the verdict.
kill_experiment_critique: Stage 0 as written cannot fail for the right reason and can pass for the wrong one: (1) kappa_3 >= 0.08 is inside the bid-ask-bounce band on Kraken alts (0.02-0.08 of a 12.5% shock), so a PASS is uninformative without a skip-day (t+1 entry) control and a liquidity-tercile read — Cox-Peterson 1994 is the template for why. (2) The event conjunction is effectively range-only (VZ >= 2 = 7.4x median volume is rare; RZ >= 2 is implied by the shock), so 'range OR volume' vs the bare |z_e| >= 2.5 set will read identical — the sensitivity grid has fewer real cells than 36 and the RC p-value over 36 is optimistic in the other direction (near-duplicate cells). (3) Cost is scored at 21/30 bp calibrated for calm-day daily rebalances; the mechanism trades ONLY on 2.5-sigma, 2x-range days, outside slip5's domain. The 1-minute table can supply a shock-day cost proxy (last-15-min VWAP vs close; last-minute range); it should be pre-registered, and the pass band should be stated at that cost, not at 21. (4) Stage 1 (b): 'hold-out >= +0.56 AND placebo pct >= 95 AND RC p <= 0.10' — placebo Sharpes share the book's SE (~0.8-1.0 at the bar with lumpy returns), so pct95 ~ +1.3..+1.6 is the binding requirement; power ~35-40% if the mechanism is exactly at the bar. (c): full-span CI lo > 0 includes 2019-23 where kappa, lambda, delta and caps were fitted — a contaminated confirmation; the design admits 'partial conflation' but keeps it as a PASS leg. Together (b)+(c) mean no PASS outcome satisfies 'unseen years, CI lo > 0'. (5) The cascade arm (>= 10-15 cohorts/yr at kappa 0.2) has ~20 hold-out cohorts -> t ~1.4; it should be labelled unverifiable rather than given a pass band. (6) The hedged Arm A needs a MARKET control: long-BTC-after-cascade (breadth 1). If the hedged book is positive and the BTC-only control is positive, the source is market reversal via beta error (shrunk beta on -15% days), not residual liquidity provision; the design's hedged-vs-unhedged pair does not separate these. (7) Delisting tail: exit 'at close t+h' is undefined when an asset stops printing inside h (present_mask drops dead tails); pre-register the exit price (last available close, or zero) — this decides BEAR22 for the FTX-week cohort (SRM/RAY/MNGO/OXY/FIDA are in the 273 universe). (8) Multiplicity is under-counted: 36 cells x 2 model classes x 2 arms x hedged/unhedged x 2 accountings x 2 cost tiers ~ 1,152 reads; RC covers 36. (9) Good parts worth keeping: the analytic gate (no learned abstention), hold-to-horizon (no 892 channel), the anti-HOLD cohort COUNT with a FAIL threshold, date-clustered SEs, circular-shift placebo, SR0(N) printed — these are the correct instruments and should migrate into TASK_915's SPEC appendix regardless of this design's fate.
odds_after_refutation: P(Stage 0 passes as written, kappa_3 >= 0.08, t >= 3) ~45-55% — but inflated by bounce, hence uninformative. P(kappa_3 with skip-day entry >= 0.10 on the top-liquidity tercile, t >= 3, above placebo p95) ~10-15%. P(a frozen SCRR book clears +0.97 net@21 as a POINT estimate on the 2024-01 -> 2026-06 hold-out) ~3-5%; P(it clears +0.56, the PIT line) ~8-10%. P(the goalposts as written — unseen years, CI lo > 0, BEAR22 positive, holds positions, at fee16/slip5) via this mechanism: ~1-2%, structurally under-powered (hold-out CI +-1.5 at the bar; the full-span CI is in-sample). P(any positive net edge survives a shock-day immediacy cost of 40+ bp/side) ~2-4%. Net: the design's own ~7% unconditional falls to ~1-2% for the goalposts; the Stage-0 measurement retains information value (~1 in 3 chance it changes what TASK_915 should read) as a two-hour appendix, and no independent row.
